name: John Reid
bio: A Representative from Missouri; born near Lynchburg, Bedford County, Va., June 14, 1821; attended the common schools; moved to Missouri in 1840; taught school; studied law; was admitted to the bar and commenced practice in Jefferson City, Mo., in 1844; served as captain in the Mexican War; member of the State house of representatives 1854-1856; elected as a Democrat to the Thirty-seventh Congress (March 4, 1861-December 2, 1861); withdrew from the House of Representatives on August 3, 1861; expelled from the U.S. House of Representatives on December 2, 1861, for taking up arms against the government of the United States; served in the Confederate army as volunteer aide to General Price; appointed a commissioner to adjust claims against the Confederate government; settled in Kansas City, Mo.; resumed the practice of his profession and engaged in banking; died on November 22, 1881, at Lees Summit, Jackson County, Mo.; interment in Elmwood Cemetery, Kansas City, Mo.
